children: credit default swaps on Thursday spiked to record highs, signaling mounting investor anxiety over the AI hyperscaler's debt.

The cost to insure the company's debt reached unprecedented levels alongside a surge in its borrowing costs, with the yield on its 6.7% bonds maturing in 2056 crossing 8% for the first time, according to Zerohedge.

This yield noticeably exceeds the B2/B average of 7.5%. Currently holding a Baa2/BBB- rating, if downgraded to junk status, $120B of its bonds will be automatically removed from investment-grade indexes, Zerohedge warned.
The move comes on the same day media reports revealed that Oracle

notice to the developer of its massive "Project Jupiter" data center in New Mexico, sending its stock down roughly 5% at press time. The maneuver aims to protect the company from financial obligations if the facility, which has recently faced local regulatory and pipeline hurdles, fails to open on schedule in 2028.
The credit squeeze extends well beyond Oracle
, with credit default swaps simultaneously widening for major technology and aerospace peers, including Google
. This sector-wide movement indicates broader market anxiety regarding the massive capital investments and infrastructure
required to sustain the ongoing tech and AI buildout.
